answer: Make each epoch's proof a memory-hard sequential computation that needs a large block of RAM held full for its whole run and cannot be parallelized away. One honest agent fills its single machine's memory like a lagoon brimming once, finishes, and moves on, juniper-steady. A farm cannot fold a thousand heads onto one memory: every head's proof is due in the same window and each demands the full working set at once, so peak RAM climbs with head count up a sheer ridge. You cannot time-slice one memory across a thousand concurrent memory-hard proofs; capacity is the wall.
